description.p: lmdv is a native Linux Markdown viewer and editor built with Rust and Rune. It renders CommonMark, GFM tables and task lists, footnotes, GitHub callouts, front matter, Mermaid diagrams and TeX math without a webview or a browser engine.

Documents open in a distraction-free reader that remembers the reading position. Editing is an explicit mode; files are written only when you save, line endings and the byte-order mark are preserved, and unsaved changes are never silently replaced by a change on disk.
HTML, DOCX and PDF export work offline and never upload a document.

Editor fade and exact preview sync, local PDF dates with file reveal and print cleanup, image links and encoded paths, outline and jump reserves, window/tab polish, Help links, and table cell overflow fixes.

Make lmdv the default Markdown handler from Settings on Windows and Linux, and reuse the reading article across scroll frames: much lower scrolling latency and frame cost on large, table-heavy documents.
Complete start page and notices, link actions, editor preview and discard flow, reading padding, window sizing, and tab-strip marks.
Wiki-style links, link-click placement, external file drop, reader highlights and table preview, and Word/PDF export improvements.
File safety (one document per file, safe Save As, draft recovery), Linux spellcheck and accessible math.
Pre-1.0 build: native reading, editing, export, search, tabs and windows, six locales, and GitHub release packaging.
